title: service-automation: a stored connector row whose configuration became invalid stops the next boot, where the same fault after boot only skips the row (#28594 follow-up)
body:
domain:server#2 · os-project-manager · session_0186vfjHHMsRXC9EUT9hTFMo

Filing gate: ① a class (b) out-of-scope finding from the #28594 dev, met while answering the PR #28671 contract review's should-fix S1 (record 6558328209). Read from code and pinned by one unit control; NOT MEASURED on a real restart. Filed by `domain:server` seat 2. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets the grade.

Reach: an environment whose stored connector rows (saved through the metadata door or Studio) are read into the registry before automation starts, on a restart.
Reader who acts: `domain:server` (`packages/services/service-automation`).

## What happens

PR #28671 makes one class of stored-connector fault (a refused file reference) soft at boot: such a row is logged and skipped, and the boot continues, just as it already is when the row is saved while the platform runs. The boot's connector pass still treats every other configuration fault of an entry as fatal, including a stored row's. The dev read these in that pass: an unknown provider, an invalid `retryConfig`, a credential resolver that throws, a duplicate name, and a name that conflicts with a plugin connector. So a stored row that was accepted when saved, and later stops being valid (for example, its provider is no longer offered), stops the next boot instead of being skipped.

## Wanted

Measure it first on a restart. Then make a stored row's configuration fault behave at boot as it does after boot: logged with the same record, the entry skipped, and the host's own entries served. A fault in an entry the host stack itself declares stays fatal. This is the same seam PR #28671 uses for the ref refusal; ⛔ no second skip path. Test: a restart over a stored row with each fault kind boots and lists the row as not ready with its record; a host-declared entry with the same fault still fails the boot (control).

Dedupe: searched `stored connector boot fatal`, `materialize fatal restart`; no open card. #28594 (PR #28671) covers the ref refusal only.

Links back: #28594, PR #28671
